custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create a part, part A, for this test with a Sell Price of $20.00, and set it inactive.
  • Use a desktop browser that can open a second tab on the same ShopView address, signed in as the same user.
  • Start in browser tab 1 on the Inventory page, on the Inactive tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C839449-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C839449-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
  • To set a part inactive: on the Inventory page's Active tab click Search, type its part number, click its row; in Edit Inventory Part click Inactive under Part Status, click Save, then click Deactivate in the Deactivate part? window. The part then shows on the Inactive tab.
  • Second tab: open a new browser tab on the same QA site address (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com); you stay signed in as the same user.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A in tab 1.

Step 2:

  • Sell Price shows 27.00.

Step 3:

  • Active is selected.

Step 4:

  • A second tab opens.

Step 5:

  • Tab 2 shows the Parts left menu.

Step 6:

  • Tab 2 shows the Inventory page.

Step 7:

  • The Inactive tab is selected in tab 2.

Step 8:

  • Part A is listed in tab 2.

Step 9:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens in tab 2.

Step 10:

  • Active is selected in tab 2.

Step 11:

  • The "Activate part?" confirmation opens in tab 2.

Step 12:

  • Tab 2 shows "Part activated.": part A is now active.

Step 13:

  • Tab 1 still shows the part window with Active picked.

Step 14:

  • The "Activate part?" confirmation opens in tab 1.

Step 15:

  • The confirmation stays open, and a red message reads "This part could not be activated" with the reason "Part is already in that state."

Step 16:

  • The red message is still showing after 10 seconds: it stays until it is closed.

Step 17:

  • The red message closes and the confirmation is still open.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog), story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S13-N4: “If the status change is refused after the save, the confirmation stays open and the system shows "This part could not be deactivated" or "This part could not be activated", with the reason.”
  • S10-R13a: “The reasons are "A core follows its part. Activate or deactivate the part instead.", "Part not found." and "Part is already in that state."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Status change from the part dialog refused | "This part could not be deactivated" / "This part could not be activated", with the reason | Error toast, stays until closed”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.
